chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a muqatabah (contracted slave) who committed adultery. He said: 'Look at what has been taken from her contract; that portion constitutes the penalty (hadd) of the free woman, and whatever remains unpaid constitutes the penalty (hadd) of the slave woman.'

And he said regarding a muqatabah who committed adultery, where three-quarters of her contract had been paid and one quarter remained: 'She is lashed three-quarters of the penalty of the free woman, calculated from one hundred, which is seventy-five lashes. And she is lashed one-quarter of the penalty of the slave woman, calculated from fifty, which is twelve and a half lashes. So that totals eighty-seven and a half lashes. And he refused to stone her and exile her before her emancipation is clarified.'

key_terms.حَدُّ الْأَمَةِ: The penalty for a slave woman (50 lashes)
key_terms.حَدُّ الْحُرَّةِ: The penalty for a free woman (100 lashes)
key_terms.زَنَتْ: Committed adultery (by a free or slave woman)
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٍ: Contracted slave woman who pays for her freedom in installments

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for a contracted slave woman (muqatabah) who commits adultery?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the proportional application of the hadd penalty for a muqatabah (contracted slave) who commits adultery, distinguishing between the status of the paid and unpaid portions of her manumission. This ruling reflects the juristic principle that the 'free' portion incurs the 100-lash penalty while the 'slave' portion incurs 50 lashes, resulting in a total of 87.5 lashes. Notably, the Imam explicitly withheld stoning (rajm) and exile (nafy) until her complete emancipation was verified, highlighting the precision of Shia legal methodology in applying mixed-status penalties.
